_README: INPUTS to the Gate 0 unit-economics model. Every value carries `src`: a sources.md key (verified evidence), an assumption ID from doc 01, or ASSUMPTION(...) where a figure was derived because no public source exists. Edit and re-run `node docs/homie-coffee/model/unit-economics.mjs --all`.
_vatNote: Omnomnom sp. z o.o. is NOT a VAT payer from 2026-01-01 (F12). The model therefore works entirely in GROSS costs — input VAT is not reclaimable, so the gross price paid IS the cost — and charges no output VAT, so the shelf price IS net revenue. VAT rates are consequently not model inputs. The legal position, including whether a non-VAT payer can invoice businesses without disadvantaging them, is in doc 14 and needs accountant confirmation.
_dropshipNote: Dropshipping was one of three supply routes to price out. It is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from supplyModels: no Polish coffee roaster or wholesaler was found publishing dropshipping terms on its own site (SUP-33). It cannot be modelled without inventing numbers, so it is not modelled.

contractRoastPrivateLabel.label: Contract roasting / private label, our own brand on the bag

costPerKgRoastedGross.note: Palarnia Meksyk 31 PLN/250 g. THE ONLY publicly quoted private-label price in Poland, and the source itself calls it an average. The entire gate turns on this number.

packagingIncluded.note: Meksyk supplies black doypack with zip and degassing valve, and free template label edits — so pouch and label are NOT charged again.

moqKg.note: Lafaye: 20 units per SKU, i.e. 5 kg at 250 g; zero minimum with client-supplied labels. DIFFERENT SUPPLIER from the price above — mixing them is optimistic and is flagged as such.

wholesaleResale.label: Wholesale resale of an existing roaster's product, under THEIR brand

costPerKgRoastedGross.note: NOT PUBLIC. Zero of eight wholesalers publish PLN/kg (SUP-32). Derived: Polish roaster DTC retail 125-175 PLN/kg (SUP-28) less the ~12-20% reseller discount that is published (SUP-21). Wide error bar; treat as illustrative only.

packagingIncluded.note: Supplier's own retail packaging. No wholesale programme found permits relabelling, so this route cannot build our brand.

moqKg.note: Hurtownia Kawy i Herbaty: 300 PLN net minimum order, which is roughly 2-3 kg at these prices.

leadTimeDays.note: Stocked goods ship faster than roast-to-order. Not sourced.

packagingPerBag._note: Used only when the supply model does NOT include packaging. Plain pouch plus applied label; custom-printed pouches are quote-only at every Polish producer checked, so that fork is unpriced.

pouch250g.note: Arkom, plain 250 g doypack with degassing valve, 152 PLN/100 szt at MOQ 100.

pouch1kg.note: Same supplier, 1 kg doypack with valve, 222 PLN/100 szt.

label.note: Samart digital print, 11-30 cm2, 1.00 PLN/szt at 1000 szt (netto, +23% VAT which we cannot reclaim). At 100 szt it is 2.30 PLN.

outerBoxOrMailer.note: NOT SOURCED. Outer carton, filler and tape were explicitly excluded from every cost page found; the research flagged 1-3 PLN as plausible. Sensitivity-tested in doc 05.

packMinutesPerOrder.note: Not sourced. Pick, pack, label, book the parcel.

founderHourlyOpportunityCost.note: ZERO in the base view, which shows CASH contribution only. The labour-loaded view is a scenario override, because A7 says the model must expose any full-time-founder dependency rather than hide it.

b2cParcelCost.note: Furgonetka displays 11.09 PLN netto and 15.41 PLN brutto for InPost Paczkomat gabaryt A. Omnomnom is currently VAT-exempt and cannot reclaim input VAT, so the model must use the displayed gross cash cost. The page's net/gross columns do not reconcile at 23%; verify the invoice before Gate 1.

b2cParcelPriceCharged.note: Within the observed market range: Swiezo Palona 9.90, Figa 10.00, Coffeedesk 9.99-14.99.

freeShippingThreshold.note: Median and modal Polish consumer threshold across 11 verified stores; working band 129-159.

codShareOfOrders.note: NOT SOURCED for coffee. BLIK at 72% of PL e-commerce transactions implies prepayment dominates; 10% COD is a conservative placeholder.

b2bDeliveryCostPerDrop.note: Not sourced. A local Krakow drop. Payment terms and B2B logistics pricing could not be established publicly (B2B gap).

cardFeeFixed.note: Stripe's fixed 1.00 PLN is the dominant payment cost on small Polish baskets.

blikFeeRate.note: Stripe Poland BLIK, 1.6% + 1.00 PLN. Przelewy24 (1.9%) and PayU (1.19% + 0.09) are reportedly cheaper but both official pricing pages were unreachable, so those are unverified.

blikShareOfOrders.note: BLIK was ~72% of Polish e-commerce transactions by count in Q1 2026 on NBP data.

refundAndDamageRate.note: Alsendo 2026 puts all-category Polish returns at 5-7%, but that sample is fashion-weighted and coffee has no size-fit returns. 3% is a judgement below the all-category figure; no food-specific or damage-rate benchmark exists (COST gap).

averageDiscountRate.note: Blended effect of welcome codes and promotions. Note 34% of Polish consumers buy a brand only on promotion (BM-16), so this may be badly optimistic.

b2b._note: A3 correction: a warm channel is NOT zero-CAC — sales labour, samples, delivery and account management are costed explicitly. Sizes 5/10/20 kg span an office (3-4 kg/month per 20 staff, B2B-16) to a hotel (17.6 kg/month, B2B-22).

taxModelStatus.note: Safety gate. Do not enable B2B output merely by filling priceBasis. Implement and test consistent output VAT, deductible input VAT, and buyer-effective price comparisons first.

pricePerKg.note: Polish HoReCa bean ladder: 45-65 economy, 65-95 standard gastro, 95-140 premium, 120-180+ speciality PLN/kg. The source does not state whether these figures are net or gross, so this value cannot drive a VAT comparison.

priceBasis.note: Must become 'net', 'gross', or another explicitly defined comparable basis after a real supplier/customer quote and accountant review. Until then the model must not emit B2B VAT conclusions.

vatRegistered.note: Omnomnom sp. z o.o. is NOT a VAT payer. Set true to see the B2B economics after voluntary registration.

nonVatPayerPriceHandicap.note: 1 - 1/1.23. A VAT-registered business buyer deducts input VAT from a registered supplier but has nothing to deduct from us, so our price must be ~18.7% lower to cost that buyer the same. Applied to B2B revenue only; consumers are unaffected and it is a small ADVANTAGE there.

salesHoursPerWonAccount.note: Not sourced. Prospecting, sample drop, follow-up, close.

sampleCostPerProspect.note: Not sourced. ~200 g plus delivery or a personal drop.

prospectsPerWonAccount.note: Not sourced. Implies a 20% close rate on sampled prospects.

monthlyChurnRate.note: Not sourced. Beans-only carries NO contractual lock-in, unlike the 12-36 month bundled contracts (B2B-06, B2B-19) — so churn should be assumed HIGHER than the incumbents', not lower.

assumedCpc.note: Weighted average Polish Search CPC across 4,976 campaigns. No coffee-category breakdown exists (BM gap); coffee competes against Nespresso, Lavazza, Jacobs and Allegro.

assumedConversionRate.note: Polish small-shop (<100k PLN/mo) median session conversion. Sample contains NO food category, so this may understate coffee.

repeatRateOrder2.note: NOT SOURCED. No Polish coffee repeat-rate benchmark was found. Only ~11% of Polish consumers qualify as genuinely loyal and 34% buy only on promotion (BM-16), so 30% may be generous. This is the assumption the whole business case rests on and it is the weakest number in the file.

repeatRateOrder3.note: NOT SOURCED. Conditional on having ordered twice.

validationBudgetCeilings._note: A2. Scenario ceilings, NOT committed budgets. The rejected 40-60k PLN figure must never reappear.
